sanskrit: atha lokeśvarotsṛṣṭā tatra kālena kena cit nidrā samabhavat tīvrā kumbhakarṇasya rūpiṇī
english: Then, in the course of time, Sleep in embodied form — sent by Lokeśvara himself — came upon Kumbhakarṇa with great intensity.

sanskrit: tato bhrātaram āsīnaṃ kumbhakarṇo 'bravīd vacaḥ nidrā māṃ bādhate rājan kārayasva mamālayam
english: Then Kumbhakarṇa spoke to his brother who was seated: "Sleep overpowers me, O king; have a dwelling built for me."

sanskrit: viniyuktās tato rājñā śilpino viśvakarmavat akurvan kumbhakarṇasya kailāsasamam ālayam
english: Thereupon craftsmen appointed by the king, skilled as Viśvakarman himself, constructed for Kumbhakarṇa a dwelling equal to Kailāsa.

sanskrit: vistīrṇaṃ yojanaṃ śubhraṃ tato dviguṇam āyatam darśanīyaṃ nirābādhaṃ kumbhakarṇasya cakrire
english: A yojana in breadth, twice that in length, beautiful to behold and free from any hindrance — such was the dwelling they made for Kumbhakarṇa.

sanskrit: sphāṭikaiḥ kāñcanaiś citraiḥ stambhaiḥ sarvatra śobhitam vaidūryakṛtaśobhaṃ ca kiṅkiṇījālakaṃ tathā
english: Adorned throughout with variegated columns of crystal and gold, radiant with vaidūrya gems, and hung with networks of tiny bells —

sanskrit: dantatoraṇavinyastaṃ vajrasphaṭikavedikam sarvartusukhadaṃ nityaṃ meroḥ puṇyāṃ guhām iva
english: — fitted with gateways of ivory, its terraces of diamond and crystal, pleasant in every season, it was like the sacred cave of Mount Meru.

sanskrit: tatra nidrāṃ samāviṣṭaḥ kumbhakarṇo niśācaraḥ bahūny abdasahasrāṇi śayāno nāvabudhyate
english: There the night-roaming Kumbhakarṇa, overtaken by sleep, lay slumbering for many thousands of years without awakening.

sanskrit: nidrābhibhūte tu tadā kumbhakarṇe daśānanaḥ devarṣiyakṣagandharvān bādhate sma sa nityaśaḥ
english: While Kumbhakarṇa lay thus overwhelmed by sleep, the ten-headed Rāvaṇa perpetually harassed gods, seers, yakṣas, and gandharvas.

sanskrit: udyānāni vicitrāṇi nandanādīni yāni ca tāni gatvā susaṃkruddho bhinatti sma daśānanaḥ
english: The ten-headed one, filled with fierce anger, would go to the variegated pleasure-groves — Nandana and the rest — and ravage them.

sanskrit: nadīṃ gaja iva krīḍan vṛkṣān vāyur iva kṣipan nagān vajra iva sṛṣṭo vidhvaṃsayati nityaśaḥ
english: Like an elephant sporting in a river, like the wind scattering trees, like a thunderbolt hurled against mountains, he continually laid waste to all.

sanskrit: tathā vṛttaṃ tu vijñāya daśagrīvaṃ dhaneśvaraḥ kulānurūpaṃ dharmajña vṛttaṃ saṃsmṛtya cātmanaḥ
english: Having learned of the conduct of the ten-headed one, O knower of dharma, the lord of wealth Kubera recalled the conduct befitting his own lineage —

sanskrit: saubhrātradarśanārthaṃ tu dūtaṃ vaiśvaraṇas tadā laṅkāṃ saṃpreṣayām āsa daśagrīvasya vai hitam
english: — and for the sake of fraternal guidance, and for Rāvaṇa's own welfare, Vaiśravaṇa dispatched a messenger to Laṅkā.

sanskrit: sa gatvā nagarīṃ laṅkām āsasāda vibhīṣaṇam mānitas tena dharmeṇa pṛṣṭhaś cāgamanaṃ prati
english: He went to the city of Laṅkā and met Vibhīṣaṇa; honored by him with due courtesy and asked about the purpose of his coming,

sanskrit: pṛṣṭvā ca kuśalaṃ rājño jñātīn api ca bāndhavān sabhāyāṃ darśayām āsa tam āsīnaṃ daśānanam
english: — he inquired after the welfare of the king and of kinsmen and relatives, and then had himself presented in the assembly before the seated ten-headed Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: sa dṛṣṭvā tatra rājānaṃ dīpyamānaṃ svatejasā jayena cābhisaṃpūjya tūṣṇīm āsīn muhūrtakam
english: Seeing the king there blazing with his own splendor, the messenger honored him with words of victory and then remained silent for a moment.

sanskrit: tasyopanīte paryaṅke varāstaraṇasaṃvṛte upaviśya daśagrīvaṃ dūto vākyam athābravīt
english: Seated upon a couch that was brought forward, covered with a choice spread, the messenger then spoke these words to the ten-headed one:

sanskrit: rājan vadāmi te sarvaṃ bhrātā tava yad abravīt ubhayoḥ sadṛśaṃ saumya vṛttasya ca kulasya ca
english: "O king, I convey to you everything your brother said — words befitting both of you, O gentle one, in terms of conduct and lineage.

sanskrit: sādhu paryāptam etāvat kṛtaś cāritrasaṃgrahaḥ sādhu dharme vyavasthānaṃ kriyatāṃ yadi śakyate
english: 'Enough of this — you have had sufficient sport and made your display of conduct. It is good to establish oneself in dharma, if that be possible.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭaṃ me nandanaṃ bhagnam ṛṣayo nihatāḥ śrutāḥ devānāṃ tu samudyogas tvatto rājañ śrutaś ca me
english: 'I have seen Nandana broken; I hear that seers have been slain. And I have heard of the gods' mobilization against you, O king.

sanskrit: nirākṛtaś ca bahuśas tvayāhaṃ rākṣasādhipa aparāddhā hi bālyāc ca rakṣaṇīyāḥ svabāndhavāḥ
english: 'I have been dismissed by you many times, O lord of rākṣasas. Yet one must protect one's own kinsmen even when they offend, for it is the nature of kinship.

sanskrit: ahaṃ tu himavatpṛṣṭhaṃ gato dharmam upāsitum raudraṃ vrataṃ samāsthāya niyato niyatendriyaḥ
english: 'I, for my part, went to the slopes of the Himālaya to practice dharma, undertaking the severe vrata of Rudra, disciplined and with senses restrained.

sanskrit: tatra devo mayā dṛṣṭaḥ saha devyomayā prabhuḥ savyaṃ cakṣur mayā caiva tatra devyāṃ nipātitam
english: 'There I beheld the god, the Lord, together with the goddess Umā. And my left eye fell upon the goddess —

sanskrit: kā nv iyaṃ syād iti śubhā na khalv anyena hetunā rūpaṃ hy anupamaṃ kṛtvā tatra krīḍati pārvatī
english: '— with the thought "who might this auspicious one be?" and for no other reason, for Pārvatī was playing there having taken on a form of incomparable beauty.

sanskrit: tato devyāḥ prabhāvena dagdhaṃ savyaṃ mamekṣaṇam reṇudhvastam iva jyotiḥ piṅgalatvam upāgatam
english: 'By the power of the goddess, my left eye was then scorched — its light extinguished as by dust, it became tawny in color.

sanskrit: tato 'ham anyad vistīrṇaṃ gatvā tasya gires taṭam pūrṇaṃ varṣaśatāny aṣṭau samavāpa mahāvratam
english: 'Then I went to another vast slope of that mountain, and performed the great vrata there for eight full hundreds of years.

sanskrit: samāpte niyame tasmiṃs tatra devo maheśvaraḥ prītaḥ prītena manasā prāha vākyam idaṃ prabhuḥ
english: 'When that observance was complete, the great god Maheśvara, the Lord, pleased, with a glad heart spoke these words:

sanskrit: prīto 'smi tava dharmajña tapasānena suvrata mayā caitad vrataṃ cīrṇaṃ tvayā caiva dhanādhipa
english: '"I am pleased with you, O knower of dharma, O one of excellent vow, through this austerity. This vrata has been performed both by me and by you, O lord of wealth.

sanskrit: tṛtīyaḥ puruṣo nāsti yaś cared vratam īdṛśam vrataṃ suduścaraṃ hy etan mayaivotpāditaṃ purā
english: '"There is no third person who has performed such a vrata; this vrata, most difficult to undertake, was originated by me alone in former times.

sanskrit: tat sakhitvaṃ mayā sārdhaṃ rocayasva dhaneśvara tapasā nirjitatvād dhi sakhā bhava mamānagha
english: '"Therefore, be pleased to accept friendship with me, O lord of wealth. By your austerity you have overcome all — be my friend, O sinless one.

sanskrit: devyā dagdhaṃ prabhāvena yac ca sāvyaṃ tavekṣaṇam ekākṣi piṅgalety eva nāma sthāsyati śāśvatam
english: '"And that left eye of yours which was scorched by the power of the goddess — you shall be called for eternity Ekākṣipiṅgala, 'the tawny one-eyed.'"

sanskrit: evaṃ tena sakhitvaṃ ca prāpyānujñāṃ ca śaṃkarāt āgamya ca śruto 'yaṃ me tava pāpaviniścayaḥ
english: 'Having thus obtained friendship and leave from Śaṃkara, and upon returning, I have heard of your wicked resolve.'

sanskrit: tadadharmiṣṭhasaṃyogān nivarta kuladūṣaṇa cintyate hi vadhopāyaḥ sarṣisaṃghaiḥ surais tava
english: 'Therefore, turn back from these most unrighteous associations, O defiler of your lineage — for the gods together with hosts of seers are devising the means of your destruction.'

sanskrit: evam ukto daśagrīvaḥ kruddhaḥ saṃraktalocanaḥ hastān dantāṃś a saṃpīḍya vākyam etad uvāca ha
english: Addressed thus, the ten-headed Rāvaṇa, enraged with red-suffused eyes, grinding his hands and teeth together, spoke these words:

sanskrit: vijñātaṃ te mayā dūta vākyaṃ yat tvaṃ prabhāṣase naiva tvam asi naivāsau bhrātrā yenāsi preṣitaḥ
english: "I have understood the words you are speaking, O messenger. You are not what you appear, nor is he truly my brother who has sent you.

sanskrit: hitaṃ na sa mamaitad dhi bravīti dhanarakṣakaḥ maheśvarasakhitvaṃ tu mūḍha śrāvayase kila
english: "The guardian of wealth does not speak this for my benefit. And you, fool, presume to make me hear of his friendship with Maheśvara!

sanskrit: na hantavyo gurur jyeṣṭho mamāyam iti manyate tasya tv idānīṃ śrutvā me vākyam eṣā kṛtā matiḥ
english: "He thinks: 'this elder, this senior, must not be slain by me.' But now, having heard my response, this is the resolve I have formed regarding him:

sanskrit: trīṃl lokān api jeṣyāmi bāhuvīryam upāśritaḥ etan muhūrtam eṣo 'haṃ tasyaikasya kṛte ca vai caturo lokapālāṃs tān nayiṣyāmi yamakṣayam
english: "I shall conquer all three worlds relying on the strength of my arms! And this very moment, solely on his account, I shall lead the four Lokapālas to the realm of Yama."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu laṅkeśo dūtaṃ khaḍgena jaghnivān dadau bhakṣayituṃ hy enaṃ rākṣasānāṃ durātmanām
english: Having spoken thus, the lord of Laṅkā struck the messenger with his sword and gave him over to his wicked rākṣasas to be devoured.

sanskrit: tataḥ kṛtasvastyayano ratham āruhya rāvaṇaḥ trailokyavijayākāṅkṣī yayau tatra dhaneśvaraḥ
english: Then Rāvaṇa, having had auspicious rites performed, mounted his chariot desiring the conquest of the three worlds, and set forth toward Kubera, the lord of wealth.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa sacivaiḥ sārdhaṃ ṣaḍbhir nityaṃ balotkaṭaiḥ mahodaraprahastābhyāṃ mārīcaśukasāraṇaiḥ
english: Then he set out with his six ministers, ever mighty in their strength — Mahodara, Prahasta, Mārīca, Śuka, and Sāraṇa —

sanskrit: dhūmrākṣeṇa ca vīreṇa nityaṃ samaragṛdhnunā vṛtaḥ saṃprayayau śrīmān krodhāl lokān dahann iva
english: — and the valiant Dhūmrākṣa, ever eager for battle; accompanied thus, the glorious one marched forth, burning the worlds as it were with his wrath.

sanskrit: purāṇi sa nadīḥ śailān vanāny upavanāni ca atikramya muhūrtena kailāsaṃ girim āviśat
english: Passing over cities, rivers, mountains, forests, and groves in but a moment, he entered Mount Kailāsa.

sanskrit: taṃ niviṣṭaṃ girau tasmin rākṣasendraṃ niśamya tu rājño bhrātāyam ity uktvā gatā yatra dhaneśvaraḥ
english: On hearing that the lord of rākṣasas had encamped on that mountain, the guards said "this is the king's brother" and went to where the lord of wealth Kubera was.

sanskrit: gatvā tu sarvam ācakhyur bhrātus tasya viniścayaḥ anujñātā yayuś caiva yuddhāya dhanadena te
english: Having gone, they reported to him the entire resolve of his brother; and being authorized by Kubera, they went forth to battle.

sanskrit: tato balasya saṃkṣobhaḥ sāgarasyeva vardhataḥ abhūn nairṛtarājasya giriṃ saṃcālayann iva
english: Then the stirring of the Nairṛta king's army grew like the swelling of the ocean, shaking the mountain as it were.

sanskrit: tato yuddhaṃ samabhavad yakṣarākṣasasaṃkulam vyathitāś cābhavaṃs tatra sacivās tasya rakṣasaḥ
english: Then a battle broke out, thick with yakṣas and rākṣasas; and the ministers of that rākṣasa lord were hard pressed there.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā tādṛśaṃ sainyaṃ daśagrīvo niśācaraḥ harṣān nādaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā roṣāt samabhivartata
english: Seeing his army in such a state, the night-roaming Rāvaṇa let out a shout of exhilaration and advanced in fury.

sanskrit: ye tu te rākṣasendrasya sacivā ghoravikramaḥ te sahasraṃ sahasrāṇām ekaikaṃ samayodhayan
english: Those ministers of the lord of rākṣasas, terrible in their valor, each fought a thousand thousands of the enemy.

sanskrit: tato gadābhiḥ parighair asibhiḥ śaktitomaraiḥ vadhyamāno daśagrīvas tat sainyaṃ samagāhata
english: Then Rāvaṇa, even while being struck down with clubs, iron bars, swords, spears, and tomaras, plunged into that army.

sanskrit: tair nirucchvāsavat tatra vadhyamāno daśānanaḥ varṣamāṇair iva ghanair yakṣendraiḥ saṃnirudhyata
english: The ten-headed one, being battered there as though breathless, was hemmed in on all sides by the lords of yakṣas who rained blows upon him like storm-clouds.

sanskrit: sa durātmā samudyamya kāladaṇḍopamāṃ gadām praviveśa tataḥ sainyaṃ nayan yakṣān yamakṣayam
english: That evil one then raised his mace, equal to the rod of Kāla, and plunged into the army, sending yakṣas to the realm of Yama.

sanskrit: sa kakṣam iva vistīrṇaṃ śuṣkendhanasamākulam vātenāgnir ivāyatto 'dahat sainyaṃ sudāruṇam
english: Like fire driven by the wind burning a vast expanse of dry kindling, he burned that army most terribly.

sanskrit: tais tu tasya mṛdhe 'mātyair mahodaraśukādibhiḥ alpāvaśiṣṭās te yakṣāḥ kṛtā vātair ivāmbudāḥ
english: By those ministers of his in battle — Mahodara, Śuka, and the rest — the yakṣas were reduced to a remnant, like clouds scattered by the wind.

sanskrit: ke cit tv āyudhabhagnāṅgāḥ patitāḥ samarakṣitau oṣṭhān svadaśanais tīkṣṇair daṃśanto bhuvi pātitāḥ
english: Some, their limbs broken by weapons, fell in the field of battle, biting their lips with their own sharp teeth as they were cast to the ground.

sanskrit: bhayād anyonyam āliṅgya bhraṣṭaśastrā raṇājire niṣedus te tadā yakṣāḥ kūlā jalahatā iva
english: Overcome by fear, their weapons fallen away, those yakṣas then sat upon the battleground embracing one another, like river banks battered by water.

sanskrit: hatānāṃ svargasaṃsthānāṃ yudhyatāṃ pṛthivītale prekṣatām ṛṣisaṃghānāṃ na babhūvāntaraṃ divi
english: For those slain and established in heaven, for those still fighting on earth, for the hosts of seers watching from above — there was no distinction between heaven and earth.

sanskrit: etasminn antare rāma vistīrṇabalavāhanaḥ agamat sumahān yakṣo nāmnā saṃyodhakaṇṭakaḥ
english: At that moment, O Rāma, a very mighty yakṣa named Saṃyodhakaṇṭaka came forward, commanding vast forces and conveyances.

sanskrit: tena yakṣeṇa mārīco viṣṇuneva samāhataḥ patitaḥ pṛthivīṃ bheje kṣīṇapuṇya ivāmbarāt
english: Struck by that yakṣa as though by Viṣṇu himself, Mārīca fell and touched the earth, like one whose merit is exhausted falling from the sky.

sanskrit: prāptasaṃjño muhūrtena viśramya ca niśācaraḥ taṃ yakṣaṃ yodhayām āsa sa ca bhagnaḥ pradudruve
english: Having regained his senses after a moment and rested, the night-roamer again engaged that yakṣa in combat; and the yakṣa, routed, fled.

sanskrit: tataḥ kāñcanacitrāṅgaṃ vaidūryarajatokṣitam maryādāṃ dvārapālānāṃ toraṇaṃ tat samāviśat
english: Then he entered the gateway that marked the boundary of the gatekeepers — ornamented with gold, dappled with vaidūrya and silver.

sanskrit: tato rāma daśagrīvaṃ praviśantaṃ niśācaram sūryabhānur iti khyāto dvārapālo nyavārayat
english: Then, O Rāma, as the night-roaming Rāvaṇa was entering, a gatekeeper known as Sūryabhānu barred his way.

sanskrit: tatas toraṇam utpāṭya tena yakṣeṇa tāḍitaḥ rākṣaso yakṣasṛṣṭena toraṇena samāhataḥ na kṣitiṃ prayayau rāma varāt salilayoninaḥ
english: Then, having torn out the gateway, the rākṣasa was struck by that yakṣa with the gateway he had hurled — yet he did not fall to the ground, O Rāma, by virtue of the boon granted by the one born of waters.

sanskrit: sa tu tenaiva taṃ yakṣaṃ toraṇena samāhanat nādṛśyata tadā yakṣo bhasma tena kṛtas tu saḥ
english: But Rāvaṇa struck that yakṣa with that same gateway; the yakṣa was no longer seen — he had been reduced to ashes by it.

sanskrit: tataḥ pradudruvuḥ sarve yakṣā dṛṣṭvā parākramam tato nadīr guhāś caiva viviśur bhayapīḍitāḥ
english: Then all the yakṣas fled upon seeing this feat of valor, and tormented by fear they took refuge in rivers and caves.

sanskrit: tatas tān vidrutān dṛṣṭvā yakṣāñ śatasahasraśaḥ svayam eva dhanādhyakṣo nirjagāma raṇaṃ prati
english: Then, seeing those yakṣas fleeing in their hundreds of thousands, the superintendent of wealth Kubera himself came forth to battle.

sanskrit: tatra māṇicāro nāma yakṣaḥ paramadurjayaḥ vṛto yakṣasahasraiḥ sa caturbhiḥ samayodhayan
english: There a yakṣa named Māṇicāra, supremely difficult to conquer, encircled by four thousand yakṣas, gave battle.

sanskrit: te gadāmusalaprāsaśaktitomaramudgaraiḥ abhighnanto raṇe yakṣā rākṣasān abhidudruvuḥ
english: Those yakṣas, striking with clubs, pestles, javelins, śaktis, tomaras, and iron hammers in battle, rushed upon the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: tataḥ prahastena tadā sahasraṃ nihataṃ raṇe mahodareṇa gadayā sahasram aparaṃ hatam
english: Then Prahasta slew a thousand in battle, and Mahodara with his mace slew another thousand.

sanskrit: kruddhena ca tadā rāma mārīcena durātmanā nimeṣāntaramātreṇa dve sahasre nipātite
english: And the wicked Mārīca in his rage, O Rāma, felled two thousand in merely the interval of a blink.

sanskrit: dhūmrākṣeṇa samāgamya māṇibhadro mahāraṇe musalenorasi krodhāt tāḍito na ca kampitaḥ
english: Engaging Dhūmrākṣa in the great battle, Māṇibhadra struck him on the chest with a pestle in fury — yet he did not waver.

sanskrit: tato gadāṃ samāvidhya māṇibhadreṇa rākṣasaḥ dhūmrākṣas tāḍito mūrdhni vihvalo nipapāta ha
english: Then Māṇibhadra, swinging his mace, struck the rākṣasa Dhūmrākṣa on the head; overcome, he fell.

sanskrit: dhūmrākṣaṃ tāḍitaṃ dṛṣṭvā patitaṃ śoṇitokṣitaḥ abhyadhāvat susaṃkruddho māṇibhadraṃ daśānanaḥ
english: Seeing Dhūmrākṣa struck down and fallen, drenched in blood, the ten-headed Rāvaṇa charged at Māṇibhadra in great fury.

sanskrit: taṃ kruddham abhidhāvantaṃ yugāntāgnim ivotthitam śaktibhis tāḍayām āsa tisṛbhir yakṣapuṃgavaḥ
english: That foremost of yakṣas struck him — charging in fury like the fire at the world's end — with three śaktis.

sanskrit: tato rākṣasarājena tāḍito gadayā raṇe tasya tena prahāreṇa mukuṭaḥ pārśvam āgataḥ tadā prabhṛti yakṣo 'sau pārśvamaulir iti smṛtaḥ
english: But then struck by the king of rākṣasas with his mace in battle, that blow caused his crown to fall to his side; from that time forward that yakṣa was remembered as Pārśvamauli, 'he whose crown is at his side.'

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tu vimukhe yakṣe māṇibhadre mahātmani saṃnādaḥ sumahān rāma tasmiñ śaile vyavardhata
english: With that great-souled yakṣa Māṇibhadra having turned back, O Rāma, a tremendous uproar grew on that mountain.

sanskrit: tato dūrāt pradadṛśe dhanādhyakṣo gadādharaḥ śukraproṣṭaḥpadābhyāṃ ca śaṅkhapadmasamāvṛtaḥ
english: Then from afar appeared the lord of wealth, mace in hand, accompanied by Śukra and Proṣṭhapada, surrounded by the treasure-keepers Śaṅkha and Padma.

sanskrit: sa dṛṣṭvā bhrātaraṃ saṃkhye śāpād vibhraṣṭagauravam uvāca vacanaṃ dhīmān yuktaṃ paitāmahe kule
english: Seeing his brother in battle — his dignity forfeited by the curse — the wise one spoke words befitting the lineage of their grandsire Brahmā:

sanskrit: mayā tvaṃ vāryamāṇo 'pi nāvagacchasi durmate paścād asya phalaṃ prāpya jñāsyase nirayaṃ gataḥ
english: "Though you are restrained by me, you do not understand, O wicked one. Having experienced the fruit of this hereafter, you will come to know it when you are gone to hell.

sanskrit: yo hi mohād viṣaṃ pītvā nāvagacchati mānavaḥ pariṇāme sa vi mūḍho jānīte karmaṇaḥ phalam
english: "Indeed, the man who out of delusion drinks poison and does not understand — that fool comes to know the fruit of his action only at the end.

sanskrit: daivatāni hi nandanti dharmayuktena kena cit yena tvam īdṛśaṃ bhāvaṃ nītas tac ca na budhyase
english: "The gods rejoice in one who is endowed with dharma; it is by that dharma that you have been brought to this state — yet this you do not comprehend.

sanskrit: yo hi mātṝḥ pitṝn bhrātṝn ācaryāṃś cāvamanyate sa paśyati phalaṃ tasya pretarājavaśaṃ gataḥ
english: "Indeed, he who disrespects mothers, fathers, brothers, and teachers — the fruit of that is seen when he has come under the power of the king of the dead.

sanskrit: adhruve hi śarīre yo na karoti tapo 'rjanam sa paścāt tapyate mūḍho mṛto dṛṣṭvātmano gatim
english: "In this transient body, he who does not accumulate austerity — that fool suffers afterward, having seen his own destination after death.

sanskrit: kasya cin na hi durbudheś chandato jāyate matiḥ yādṛśaṃ kurute karma tādṛśaṃ phalam aśnute
english: "For no one of corrupt intelligence gains good understanding by his own will; whatever action one performs, such is the fruit one reaps.

sanskrit: buddhiṃ rūpaṃ balaṃ vittaṃ putrān māhātmyam eva ca prapnuvanti narāḥ sarvaṃ svakṛtaiḥ pūrvakarmabhiḥ
english: "Men obtain all things — intelligence, beauty, strength, wealth, sons, and greatness — through their own past deeds and prior actions.

sanskrit: evaṃ nirayagāmī tvaṃ yasya te matir īdṛśī na tvāṃ samabhibhāṣiṣye durvṛttasyaiṣa nirṇayaḥ
english: "Thus you are bound for hell, one whose mind is such as this. I shall speak with you no more — this is the verdict for one of wicked conduct."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tatas tena tasyāmātyāḥ samāhatāḥ mārīcapramukhāḥ sarve vimukhā vipradudruvuḥ
english: Having spoken thus, Kubera struck down Rāvaṇa's ministers; all of them, with Mārīca at their head, turned back and fled in all directions.

sanskrit: tatas tena daśagrīvo yakṣendreṇa mahātmanā gadayābhihato mūrdhni na ca sthānād vyakampata
english: Then the ten-headed Rāvaṇa was struck on the head by that great-souled lord of yakṣas with his mace — yet he did not flinch from his position.

sanskrit: tatas tau rāma nighnantāv anyonyaṃ paramāhave na vihvalau na ca śrāntau babhūvatur amarṣaṇaiḥ
english: Then those two, O Rāma, striking each other in the supreme battle, were neither overcome nor wearied, both consumed with indignation.

sanskrit: āgneyam astraṃ sa tato mumoca dhanado raṇe vāruṇena daśagrīvas tad astraṃ pratyavārayat
english: Then Kubera, the lord of wealth, released the Āgneya weapon in battle; the ten-headed Rāvaṇa countered that weapon with the Vāruṇa weapon.

sanskrit: tato māyāṃ praviṣṭaḥ sa rākṣasīṃ rākṣaseśvaraḥ jaghāna mūrdhni dhanadaṃ vyāvidhya mahatīṃ gadām
english: Then the lord of rākṣasas, having entered into his rākṣasa illusion, whirled his great mace and struck Kubera on the head.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa tenābhihato vihvalaḥ śoṇitokṣitaḥ kṛttamūla ivāśoko nipapāta dhanādhipaḥ
english: Thus struck by him, overcome and drenched in blood, the lord of wealth fell like an aśoka tree with its roots severed.

sanskrit: tataḥ padmādibhis tatra nidhibhiḥ sa dhanādhipaḥ nandanaṃ vanam ānīya dhanado śvāsitas tadā
english: Then the lord of wealth was revived there by the treasure-keepers — Padma and the rest — who bore Kubera to the Nandana forest.

sanskrit: tato nirjitya taṃ rāma dhanadaṃ rākṣasādhipaḥ puṣpakaṃ tasya jagrāha vimānaṃ jayalakṣaṇam
english: Then, having conquered Kubera the lord of wealth, O Rāma, the lord of rākṣasas seized his Puṣpaka aerial chariot, the token of victory.

sanskrit: kāñcanastambhasaṃvītaṃ vaidūryamaṇitoraṇam muktājālapraticchannaṃ sarvakāmaphaladrumam
english: Encircled with golden pillars, its gateways set with vaidūrya gems, covered with networks of pearls, adorned with trees granting every wish —

sanskrit: tat tu rājā samāruhya kāmagaṃ vīryanirjitam jitvā vaiśravaṇaṃ devaṃ kailāsād avarohata
english: — that chariot, swift as desire and won by valor: the king mounted it and, having conquered the divine Vaiśravaṇa, descended from Kailāsa.
